new-york-hudson-valley-rides-appalachian.story: A rider’s loop: clean exit, memorable middle, calm return. A 660 km loop that starts and ends near West Long Branch, about 12 h of riding. On the way it passes Dover Beaches North and Wurtsboro. The climbs: near Saint James, Scenic stretch near Fort Salonga and in Crandon Lakes.

sections.from: Fuel stop near West Long Branch

sections.advice: This High point near Saint James → Scenic stretch near Fort Salonga stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

sections.to: Near Wurtsboro, on the way back
sections.advice: Scenic stretch near Fort Salonga → Near Wurtsboro, on the way back is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

sections.from: Near Wurtsboro, on the way back

sections.advice: Photo stop in Crandon Lakes → Mott Haven can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.

scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 80 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.
